hypothesis: One globally frozen convex mixture of C0_SCORE_PL and N1_CONDITIONAL can reduce worst-world synthetic KL across W0-W4 without prediction-time world identity or per-world retuning.
input_dataset: Digital Twin only. Design seed 20260914, 240 races/world; one-shot evaluation seed 20260915, 480 races/world. No real/historical race input, RESULT/PAYOUT, odds, economics, or holdout evidence.
prediction_method: Eleven preregistered global weights over P_mix=(1-w)C0+wN1. Design selected at most one winner by minimax KL/no-material-regression gates. Frozen weight 0.05 was evaluated once on the disjoint synthetic evaluation seed with no retune.
conclusion: FAIL. The 5% N1 mixture looked slightly minimax-better on the design seed and froze correctly, but its independent synthetic evaluation missed the strict worst-world gate: W4 max KL was 0.54052993 versus C0 0.54047717. Mean KL improved slightly and no world materially regressed, but the preregistered all-required rule correctly prevents promotion of this near-miss. No universal global mixture is established.
scientific_implication: Because matched W0-W4 races share the same PRE construction while the hidden outcome mechanism changes by world, repeated failure of universal architecture/mixing suggests an identifiability limitation: prediction-time PRE may not contain information that distinguishes the hidden stress regime. This must be audited directly before inventing more adaptive selectors.
follow_up: Run a synthetic PRE-identifiability audit for W0-W4 before any further adaptive-selector design. If world mechanism is not encoded in PRE, record that limitation and move to a separately versioned learnable-regime Digital Twin rather than post-hoc selector tuning. No real model promotion or economics claim.
